problem:
The triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dx\,dy
$$

is defined over the type I region $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le {y}^{2},\,-2\le y\le 4,\,0\le z\le 1+xy}.
$$

What is $a+b?$
worked_solution:
A type I region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(x,y)\le z\le {u}_{2}(x,y)}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type I region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/1bd4b6d0b1aa955921c1f7855d3fbd95417072a67504d9de9be44dfbbed592e5.png)

 

If $R$ is a type I region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(x,y)=0,\,{u}_{2}(x,y)=1+xy.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1+xy}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA.
$$

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le {y}^{2},\,-2\le y\le 4}.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dA & ={\int }_{-2}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{1+xy}f(x,y,z)\,dz]dx\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{1+xy}f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dx\,dy.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=-2+4=2.
$$
